doc.title: John LaPorta interviewed by Monk Rowe, Sarasota, Florida, April 13, 1996

chapter: Early bands and the swing era
title: Bob Chester and Buddy Williams bands, lead alto and Lance's Merry-Go-Round
summary: He was on the road with Bob Chester before Woody Herman, took up lead alto in Buddy Williams's Philadelphia band, and played Dayton broadcasts on WLW.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money

blocks.x: Amazing. But you started with Woody Herman at a pretty young age, right?
Well I was 24, but I’d already been on the road with Bob Chester for about two years.
Oh, playing alto at that time.
It was a band in Philadelphia by the name of Buddy Williams that, he got stuck for lead alto and he asked me about it. I says well I’ll take a crack at it. And that’s when I got the
Jimmy Dorsey alto cigar cutter. Wonderful instrument. And started playing lead alto for him and then kept it up for twenty years.
What kind of events, were they dances mostly that you played for when you were on the road with that kind of thing?

Well they varied. We played — with Buddy Williams, Bill Harris was in the band then and Eric Kluger, I don’t know whether you know that name, he was quite a well known drummer. We played in Dayton in a place called Lance’s Merry-Go-Round Bar. And WLW used to be a famous radio station that had national coverage, it had the largest range of any radio station then. They used to have nightly broadcasts so it was a really good place for a band to play. So we played there for two months on different occasions and then the band broke up. A lot of the people went into the service, the second world war, and then some of the people started getting into some of the more well known national bands like Bob Chester and some of them went with Bill, and three of the trombone players went with Benny Goodman.
